ui.tutorial.loreNote: Tap a scapegoat card, tap a tile to pencil a note, press and hold a tile until the ring fills to place them, or use 💡 Light Switch to rule out tiles. Solve the board to complete your initiation!
ui.tutorial.nudge.wrongSuspect.m: That was {name}. Use the 🧹 Eraser to lift them off, then pick {target}.
ui.tutorial.nudge.wrongSuspect.f: That was {name}. Use the 🧹 Eraser to lift them off, then pick {target}.
ui.tutorial.nudge.wrongSuspect.n: That was {name}. Use the 🧹 Eraser to lift them off, then pick {target}.
ui.tutorial.nudge.wrongTile: Not that tile — {name} belongs on the glowing one. Use the 🧹 Eraser to lift the token, then try again.
ui.tutorial.nudge.shadow: Not there — S. H. Adow hides in the only tile no one can see.
ui.tutorial.lightTile.left: Light the glowing tile to the left of {noun}.
ui.tutorial.lightTile.right: Light the glowing tile to the right of {noun}.
ui.tutorial.scripted.clearall.task: Hold the 🧹 Eraser until the ring fills.
ui.tutorial.scripted.adowDark.title: You cast no light
ui.tutorial.scripted.adowDark.text: That token is you, S. H. Adow, already on the floorplan. Look around: every tile is still in shadow. You light nothing, so you never rule a tile out and never give anyone away. Only the scapegoats switch the lights on.
ui.tutorial.scripted.adowDark.task: Tap your own card, S. H. Adow.
ui.tutorial.scripted.selectPiano.title: The easiest alibi
ui.tutorial.scripted.selectPiano.text: Start with the dullest alibi: {name} was sitting at a piano, and this house owns only one. Nobody doubts a pianist.
ui.tutorial.scripted.placeA.title: Sign for {name}
ui.tutorial.scripted.placePiano.text: Pencil whispers; a placement is a signature, so press and hold. A piano is a perch: you can sit on it, yet it stops every gaze.
ui.tutorial.scripted.placePiano.task: Hold the piano until the ring fills.
ui.tutorial.scripted.hint.title: A second opinion
ui.tutorial.scripted.hintPiano.text: The glow is {name}'s sightline, up to the palm and along to the wall. Nobody may stand in a placed scapegoat's light.
ui.tutorial.scripted.hint2.title: Put it away
ui.tutorial.scripted.hint2.text: A hint is a lamp, not a crutch. Read it, learn the pattern, then put it away: the ghost works alone.
ui.tutorial.scripted.dragB.title: Paint a trail
ui.tutorial.scripted.dragStools.text: Pencil both stools in one sweep: press on one and drag to the other. One sweep is a single Undo step.
ui.tutorial.scripted.dragStools.nudge: One tap pencils one tile. Tap it again to rub it out, then press and DRAG across both glowing stools.
ui.tutorial.scripted.rayLight.title: Lit either way
ui.tutorial.scripted.rayLight.text: Either stool {name} took, the gaze runs through the opening to the safe, so the tile beside the safe is watched: a ray block.
ui.tutorial.scripted.placeTask: Tap {name}'s card, then hold the glowing tile.
ui.tutorial.scripted.eraser.title: Lies in the light
ui.tutorial.scripted.eraserStool.text: {watcher}'s gaze lights a stool you pencilled for {name}. Nobody may stand in another's light, so that note is a lie. Rub it out.
ui.tutorial.scripted.erase1.title: Rub one out
ui.tutorial.scripted.erase1.text: Tap a pencilled tile with the Eraser and its note vanishes. One careful stroke, and the lie is gone.
ui.tutorial.scripted.eraseStool.task: Rub out the note on the glowing stool.
ui.tutorial.scripted.eraseStool.nudge: Not that one — tap the glowing stool.
ui.tutorial.scripted.undo.title: Take it back
ui.tutorial.scripted.undo.text: Second thoughts? Undo takes back your last action, even a perfect erasure (Ctrl/⌘ Z works too). A ghost may always change its mind.
ui.tutorial.scripted.erase2.title: Now mean it
ui.tutorial.scripted.eraseStool2.text: Light does not lie, and neither will your board. Rub that note out again: {name}'s gaze has made it a lie.
ui.tutorial.scripted.eraseStool2.task: Erase the note on the glowing stool again.
ui.tutorial.scripted.placeStool.title: {name} takes the last stool
ui.tutorial.scripted.placeStool.text: What survives pencil and light is the truth: one stool is left. Its gaze passes over the stove, which hides nothing.
ui.tutorial.scripted.lamp.title: Rule it out by hand
ui.tutorial.scripted.rayLamp.title: Beside the safe
ui.tutorial.scripted.rayLamp.text: Openings do not stop a gaze. No scapegoat may stand on a lit tile, and no shadow may hide there. Tap it again to switch it off.
ui.tutorial.scripted.rayLamp.nudge: Not that one — tap the glowing tile beside the safe.
ui.tutorial.scripted.placeFoot.title: {name} on the other trail
ui.tutorial.scripted.placeFoot.text: {name} stood on a trail of footprints. One is {other}'s, so only the Music Room's is left, where the Corpse hides nothing.
ui.tutorial.scripted.placeDoor.title: One opening, two tiles
ui.tutorial.scripted.placeDoor.text: {name} stood in front of an opening, in row 1. {other} sees into one side of it, so {name} takes the other.
ui.tutorial.scripted.shadow.task: Tap S. H. Adow's card, then hold the dark tile.
ui.tutorial.scripted.submit.title: Fulfil the contract
ui.tutorial.scripted.submit.text: Everyone is placed and nobody sees anyone else. Let the inspector claim his hollow victory; the ghost has already left the room.
ui.tutorial.generic.select.title: Pick a scapegoat
ui.tutorial.generic.select.text: Every soul in this room is a scapegoat, and each has a dossier card in the roster. Tap a card to pick that scapegoat up as your tool; the chosen card glows.
ui.tutorial.generic.note.title: Pencil a suspicion
ui.tutorial.generic.note.text: A good detective doubts everything. One tap on a tile pencils this scapegoat's initial in the corner, in their colour. Tap it again and the note rubs out.
ui.tutorial.generic.note.task: Tap any tile on the floorplan to write a note.
ui.tutorial.generic.paint.title: Paint a whole trail
ui.tutorial.generic.paint.text: Several tiles to rule in? Do not tap them one by one. Press on a tile and drag across the others; the whole sweep is a single Undo step.
ui.tutorial.generic.paint.task: Press on a tile and drag across a few tiles to paint notes.
ui.tutorial.generic.eraser.title: Clean the board
ui.tutorial.generic.eraser.text: Pencil lies, and so do I. The Eraser rubs out whatever you touch.
ui.tutorial.generic.erase1.title: Rub one out
ui.tutorial.generic.erase1.text: Tap a pencilled tile and its notes vanish. You can also drag the Eraser across several tiles.
ui.tutorial.generic.erase1.task: Tap a tile that has a note to erase it.
ui.tutorial.generic.undo.title: Take it back
ui.tutorial.generic.undo.text: Erased something you wanted? Nothing is final until you say so. Undo reverts your last action, one step at a time (Ctrl/⌘ Z works too).
ui.tutorial.generic.undo.task: Tap ↩️ Undo to bring the note back.
ui.tutorial.generic.clearall.title: Start from scratch
ui.tutorial.generic.clearall.text: Sometimes the whole board is a mess. Hold the Eraser down and a ring fills; keep holding until it is full and it all clears. Let go early and nothing happens.
ui.tutorial.generic.clearall.task: Press and HOLD the 🧹 Eraser until the ring fills to clear every tile.
ui.tutorial.generic.place.task: Tap {name}'s card, then press and HOLD the glowing tile until the ring fills.
ui.tutorial.generic.lights.title: Let there be light
ui.tutorial.generic.lights.text: Look at the floorplan: wherever a placed scapegoat can see, along the row or column until a wall or tall obstacle stops them, the lights switch on. A lit tile can never hold S. H. Adow, and no scapegoat may ever stand in another's light.
ui.tutorial.generic.lamp.title: The Light Switch
ui.tutorial.generic.lamp.text: Sure a tile is empty? Switch its light on by hand and stop doubting it. Lit tiles cannot hide the shadow.
ui.tutorial.generic.lamp2.title: Light a tile
ui.tutorial.generic.lamp2.text: No clue points at this tile, so nobody can be hiding here. Give it a light. Tap it again to switch the light off.
ui.tutorial.generic.hint.title: When you are stuck
ui.tutorial.generic.hint.text: Even Master U. M. Bra needs a second opinion. Ask for a hint and I will walk you through the next deduction, one step at a time.
ui.tutorial.generic.hint2.title: Put the hint away
ui.tutorial.generic.hint2.text: Read as much as you like. The deduction is yours to act on.
ui.tutorial.generic.hint2.task: Close the hint (tap Hide, ×, or 🔎 Hint again).
ui.tutorial.generic.shadow.task: Every other tile is lit. Tap S. H. Adow's card, then press and HOLD the one dark tile.
ui.tutorial.generic.submit.title: Fulfil the contract
ui.tutorial.generic.submit.text: Everyone is on the board and nobody sees anyone else. Hand your answer to the Inspector, and we shall see whether he is as foolish as I say.
ui.hero.title: The Inspectors Had It All Wrong
ui.lore.s1.1: You played the detective. You analyzed the grid. You cornered the suspects, presented your flawless logic, and patted yourself on the back when the authorities hauled them away. But did you ever wonder why the evidence always felt a little too perfect?
ui.lore.s1.2: Those bumbling fools you locked up in [[murdoku]] weren't the masterminds. They were scapegoats. The real architects of demise were never on the grid at all—they were standing right in the cracks of your logic, watching you from the dark.
ui.lore.s2.1: You are S. H. Adow, a promising initiate in the world's most elite, unseen syndicate. The deed is already done, the corpse is growing cold, and the panicked scapegoats are frantically scanning the room. Your task is not to solve the murder. Your task is to vanish.
ui.lore.s3.1: Forget the old rules. There is no neat and tidy law dictating a single scapegoat per row or column. This is a real crime scene, bounded by rigid walls, openings between areas, and towering obstacles. The scapegoats are looking everywhere—their gazes sweeping relentlessly in straight lines, passing over rugs, beds, and even the body of the victim itself. But they are flawed, and their panic creates a singular, mathematical inevitability: a blind spot.
ui.lore.s3.2: When every scapegoat is placed, one single tile remains unseen by every eye in the room. Find it, step into the shadows, and leave the scapegoats to the inspectors.
ui.show1.caption: Every scapegoat has an alibi. S. H. Adow only needs a blind spot.
ui.show2.caption: Orthogonal sightlines sweep across 7 biomes—blocked by walls and tall obstacles, passing through openings between areas.
ui.show3.caption: Every eye in the room, and still one tile no one can see. That is where you vanish.

ui.settings.plain.title: Plain directions
ui.settings.plain.desc: Replace compass words in clues with plainer ones: north of becomes above, south of becomes under, east of becomes to the right of, west of becomes to the left of.
ui.kw.beside: **Beside:** on a tile directly above, below, left or right of it, in the same room.
ui.kw.diagonal: **Diagonally next to:** on a tile touching it corner to corner, in the same room.
ui.kw.alone: **Alone:** the only person in that room. S. H. Adow cannot hide there either. Alone with someone: exactly two people in the room.
ui.kw.same: **Same room:** both stand inside the walls of one room or area.
ui.kw.only: **The only person:** nobody else is there, not even S. H. Adow.
ui.kw.exactly: **Exactly one row or column:** the next row or column over, anywhere along it.
ui.kw.north: **North of / above:** anywhere in a higher row, in any column.
ui.kw.south: **South of / under:** anywhere in a lower row, in any column.
ui.kw.east: **East of / to the right of:** anywhere in a column further right, in any row.
ui.kw.west: **West of / to the left of:** anywhere in a column further left, in any row.
ui.kw.row: **Rows:** counted from the top, so row 1 is the top row.
ui.kw.column: **Columns:** counted from the left, so column 1 is the leftmost one.
ui.kw.corner: **Corner:** a tile where two walls of the room meet at a right angle.
ui.kw.see: **Could see:** in a straight line along a row or column, with no wall, tall object or perch in between. Openings between areas let sight through.

ui.legal.title: Legal, privacy & copyright
ui.legal.intro: Last updated: 22 October 2026. Shadoku is a free puzzle game hosted at shadoku.net. For anything on this page, or any question about your data, contact us at [[email]]. This English text is the version that applies.
ui.legal.s1.p: Shadoku is free to play and provided as it is. Using the game means you accept these terms; if you do not, please do not use it.
ui.legal.s2.p: You can play without an account. Signing in with Google or GitHub is optional and lets your progress sync across devices. You are responsible for your own account, and you can delete it any time from Settings. Deleting it removes your account and the game data saved for it.
ui.legal.s3.p: In-game currency, rewards, and unlocks are just part of the game. They have no real-world value, cannot be exchanged for money, and may change as the game grows.
ui.legal.s4.p: The game is provided as it is, with no guarantees, and Shadoku is not responsible for lost progress or other indirect harm, as far as the law allows. Nothing here takes away rights your local consumer law gives you.
ui.legal.s5.p: The game and these terms may change over time. When something important changes, the date at the top will update.
ui.legal.s6.p: If you sign in, Shadoku keeps your email, display name, and avatar as Google or GitHub provides them. Your game data (puzzle progress, settings, in-game currency, and unlocks) is saved on your device and synced to Shadoku's database when you are signed in. Shadoku also uses privacy-friendly analytics, which collect general device and session information (like device type, rough region, and in-game events) to show how the game is played and help improve it. Your settings and progress are stored in your browser (localStorage), which the game needs to work.
ui.legal.s7.p: Shadoku is hosted on Cloudflare and uses OAuth authentication (Google and GitHub) and cloud database storage for sign-in, data sync, and analytics. Solution videos, if embedded, use YouTube's privacy mode (youtube-nocookie.com), which sets no tracking cookies unless you actually play a video. Links out to external communities or stores go to services with their own rules. Shadoku does not run third-party ads, though it may promote its own Shadoku puzzle books. Shadoku does not sell your data.
ui.legal.s8.p: Deleting your account in Settings removes your account and the game data saved for it. Depending on where you live, including the EU under GDPR and Brazil under LGPD, you may have extra rights to see, correct, export, or erase your data. Email [[email]] and we will help.
ui.legal.s9.p: Shadoku is a general-audience puzzle game, is not aimed at children under 13, and does not knowingly collect their data. If you think a child made an account, email us and it will be removed.
ui.legal.s10.p: The Shadoku puzzles, blindspot engine, clue text, user interface, and custom vector object art, along with translation contributions from credited collaborators, are part of the Shadoku work and are protected. Character portraits are built upon the open-source "Avataaars" system designed by Pablo Stanley (CC BY 4.0) and @dicebear/avataaars (MIT), customized for Shadoku. Copying Shadoku's original content, or building another game or app from it, is not allowed without permission. "Shadoku"™ and the Shadoku logo are trademarks of Shadoku. Questions about any of this? Email [[email]].

ui.howto.title: How to play
ui.howto.intro: Place every scapegoat on the floorplan so that each statement is true. A scapegoat switches the lights on along their row and column until a wall, the open sea or a tall prop stops the beam. No scapegoat may stand in another scapegoat's light. **S. H. Adow** hides on the one open tile left in the dark: place S there too, then press **Submit**.
ui.howto.pick: **Pick a scapegoat** by tapping their card.
ui.howto.tap: **Tap a tile** to pencil their letter in; **tap it again** to rub the note out. **Press and hold a tile** (a ring fills up) to place them for real. A placed scapegoat only comes off with the Eraser. With a keyboard, Enter writes a note and Shift+Enter places.
ui.howto.drag: **Drag** across tiles to paint notes (or wipe them, if the first tile had one).
ui.howto.props: **Not sure what a prop is?** Hover it with a mouse, or tap it on a touch screen. **Tall props** block sightlines and can never be occupied; **low props** let light pass and can be stood on. On a touch screen, low props answer only when nothing is selected: tap the selected scapegoat or tool again to put it down.
ui.howto.inspect: **📋 Inspect** lists every prop on this floorplan and whether it blocks the view and whether it can be occupied. There you can also switch off the prop info that appears when you hover a prop.
ui.howto.light: **💡 Light Switch** lights a tile by hand to rule it out as a hiding spot. Right-click it (or hold it on a touch screen) to pick the colour of your light.
ui.howto.cross: **❌ Mark X** crosses out a tile where nobody can be. A tile you cross out hides its notes; they come back when you remove the X.
ui.howto.eraser: **🧹 Eraser** clears the tiles you tap or drag over. Hold it down (a ring fills up) to clear the whole board.
ui.howto.undoHint: **↩️ Undo** takes back the last move (Ctrl/⌘ Z). **🔎 Hint** helps in three steps: where to look, the key deduction, then the placement. It also points out a mistake on your board.
ui.howto.redo: **↪️ Redo** puts back a move you undid (Ctrl/⌘ Y or Ctrl/⌘ Shift Z).
ui.howto.submit: **✅ Submit** wakes up once all scapegoats and S. H. Adow are on the board. It tells you if the contract is fulfilled or how many placements are off.
ui.howto.zoom: **− / +** (or Ctrl + mouse wheel) zooms the board and **Reset** brings the whole grid back. On a touch screen, pinch with two fingers to zoom and drag to pan.
ui.howto.rule.sight: A scapegoat **sees along their row and column** until a wall, the edge or a tall object stops the view. Openings between areas let it through.
ui.howto.rule.nosee: **No two scapegoats may see each other.** Nobody else can stand where a scapegoat can see.
ui.howto.rule.occupy: Nobody stands on **tall** or **short** objects (trees, tables). **Low** ones, like rugs, can be stood on.
ui.howto.rule.dark: With everyone placed, **exactly one tile stays dark**: that is where S. H. Adow hides.

ui.howto.adv.domino.title: Follow the sightlines.
ui.howto.adv.domino.text: Every scapegoat you place lights their row and column. Those tiles are closed to everyone else, which often leaves someone with a single tile.
ui.howto.adv.domino.example: Once the scapegoat is placed, (a) has only one tile left on the bottom row.
ui.howto.adv.rayblock.title: Block the whole line.
ui.howto.adv.rayblock.text: If every tile left for a scapegoat lies on one sightline, that line will be watched whichever tile they take.
ui.howto.adv.rayblock.example: (a) is on one of the two marked tiles. Either way, nobody else can stand on that line up to the tall object.
ui.howto.adv.law.title: Find the blind spot.
ui.howto.adv.law.text: Exactly one tile stays dark. A tile nobody can ever watch must be S. H. Adow's, and a room someone was alone in can never hide him.
ui.howto.adv.law.example: No scapegoat can still light the dark tile, so S. H. Adow is hiding there.
ui.howto.adv.trial.title: What if…?
ui.howto.adv.trial.text: On the hardest contracts, try a tile in your head: if the clues then leave someone with nowhere to stand, that tile is wrong.
ui.howto.faq.corpse.q: Does the victim count as a person?
ui.howto.faq.corpse.a: No. Nobody stands on the corpse's tile, it sees nothing, and sight passes over it.
ui.howto.faq.adow.q: Do “alone” and “the only person” include S. H. Adow?
ui.howto.faq.adow.a: Yes. Nobody else was there, so S. H. Adow cannot hide in that room or on that object either.
ui.howto.faq.true.a: Yes. Every statement and every house rule is true.
ui.howto.faq.unique.q: Is there always exactly one solution?
ui.howto.faq.unique.a: Yes. Every contract has exactly one solution.
ui.howto.faq.guess.q: Do I ever have to guess?
ui.howto.faq.guess.a: No. Every contract can be solved by logic alone. **🔎 Hint** shows one way through.
ui.howto.faq.rowcol.q: Can two scapegoats share a row or a column?
ui.howto.faq.rowcol.a: Yes, as long as a wall or a tall object stands between them, so they cannot see each other.
ui.howto.faq.doors.a: No. Sight passes through openings between areas; only walls, the edge and tall objects stop it.
ui.howto.faq.doorway.q: Can someone stand in an opening?
ui.howto.faq.doorway.a: No. An opening lies between two tiles: “in front of an opening between two areas” means on a tile beside it.
ui.howto.faq.big.q: Do big objects like a bed or a sofa count as one tile or several?
ui.howto.faq.big.a: Several: an object covers every tile it is drawn across.
ui.howto.faq.perch.q: What about a piano or a horse?
ui.howto.faq.perch.a: Someone can sit or ride on it, and it blocks sight. A sightline that reaches it from any side sees the person on it and stops there.
ui.howto.faq.portraits.q: Can I rely on the portraits?
ui.howto.faq.portraits.a: Yes. The polaroids show each scapegoat's gender, hair, glasses and hat, and clues may refer to them.
ui.about.title: About Shadoku
ui.about.lead: A murder-mystery logic puzzle where you are not the detective. You are the one who got away.
ui.about.s1.p: Every contract is a crime scene seen from above. The scapegoats stand where their alibis put them, and each of them looks along straight lines until a wall or a tall object stops their gaze. Place every scapegoat, and exactly one tile is left that no one can see: that is where S. H. Adow, the assassin, was hiding.
ui.about.s2.p: Every puzzle is built and checked by our own engine: it has exactly one solution, and you can reach it by logic alone, without guessing. The contracts grow from Very Easy to Expert, and the hints explain each deduction step by step.
ui.about.s3.p: Shadoku is a free, independent, fan-made game inspired by **[[murdoku]]**, with special thanks to **Manuel Garand** for creating it. It plays in your browser, on a phone or a computer, in many languages, with no account needed.
ui.contact.title: Contact
ui.contact.lead: A bug, a puzzle that looks wrong, a line that reads oddly in your language, or just a kind word: we read every message.
ui.contact.tips.1: Say which contract it is: its number or its title.
ui.contact.tips.2: Tell us your language and your device (phone or computer, and the browser).
ui.contact.tips.3: A screenshot helps a lot when something looks wrong.
ui.contact.reply: We answer as soon as we can.

ui.relic.case1.title: Rusted Barn Key
ui.relic.case1.desc: Knotted into the scarecrow's sleeve, for a barn that burned down years ago. Rolled tight inside its hollow shank: a torn strip of paper.
ui.relic.case2.title: Salt-Crusted Brass Token
ui.relic.case2.desc: Clenched in a fist the tide could not open. The token twists apart, and folded between its halves is a torn strip of paper.
ui.relic.case3.title: Charred Field Ledger
ui.relic.case3.desc: Its own pages went to ash, but pressed inside the burnt cover is a strip torn from another book.
ui.relic.case4.title: Stopped Silver Pocket Watch
ui.relic.case4.desc: Frozen at one o'clock, the minute the snow came down. Folded behind the dial: a torn strip of paper.
ui.relic.case5.title: Wax-Sealed Microfilm
ui.relic.case5.desc: Buried under the canyon sand in a seal of black wax. Not film at all: a strip of paper, rolled tight.
ui.relic.case6.title: Velvet Note Matchbook
ui.relic.case6.desc: From the club's own bar. One match is missing, and a torn strip of paper is folded in its place.
ui.relic.case7.title: Cracked Porcelain Half-Mask
ui.relic.case7.desc: Torn from the dancer's face as the music stopped. Glued inside the brow: a strip of paper.
ui.relic.case8.title: Hollow Silver Cartridge
ui.relic.case8.desc: Empty of powder, full of paper: one torn strip, rolled to fit the case.
ui.relic.case9.title: Pawn Shop Claim Ticket
ui.relic.case9.desc: Soaked through, but the strip of paper pinned behind it stayed dry. Whatever was pawned, nobody came back for it.
ui.relic.case10.title: Cracked Fresnel Prism
ui.relic.case10.desc: The lighthouse lens split as he fell. Wedged in the crack: a torn strip of paper.
ui.conspiracy.envelope.caption: A black envelope, sealed in cracked silver wax
ui.conspiracy.letter.title: To the apprentice
ui.conspiracy.letter.p1: Little shadow, you have been tidy. Ten contracts, ten bodies: ten Syndicate auditors, each carrying the audit eye, who had started reading your Master's private ledger.
ui.conspiracy.letter.p2: Before they died, they tore one page of that ledger into ten strips, and each of them hid one in the thing they carried. You took every piece off the bodies yourself.
ui.conspiracy.letter.p3: Lay the strips side by side until every torn edge meets its twin. The page will show you the way into your Master's manor. We will be waiting inside, uninvited, as always.
ui.conspiracy.board.title: The Evidence Board
ui.conspiracy.board.hint: Tap a strip, then another, to swap them. When every torn edge meets its twin, read the page and turn the four brass dials.
ui.conspiracy.board.whole: Every torn edge meets its twin: the page is whole again.
ui.conspiracy.unlocked.title: The brass lock springs open
ui.conspiracy.unlocked.text: The manor door swings open. Inside waits N. O. Ir, the Master's hooded second in command, carrying his private files. Two of us will be in the dark beside you.
ui.sanctum.folder.caption: Classified folder: Dossier № 000-OMEGA
ui.sanctum.lore.title: Dossier № 000-OMEGA
ui.sanctum.found: The red folder N. O. Ir carried to the end: Master U. M. Bra's own file, which nobody but the two of them was ever meant to see.
ui.sanctum.memo.head: From the desk of U. M. Bra · for N. O. Ir alone
ui.sanctum.memo.p1: N., ten auditors have opened my private ledger. Have each of them followed and photographed. I want to know where they sleep.
ui.sanctum.memo.p2: My apprentice will fulfil the contracts and believe they are Syndicate business. They are not. Nobody signs these orders but me, and the money goes where it always goes: to me.
ui.sanctum.memo.p3: When the tenth is gone, burn this file. Then close the apprentice's account as well.
ui.sanctum.photos: Ten surveillance photographs, taken before the contracts were written, each crossed out in red the day its auditor died.
ui.sanctum.lore.p1: Now you have seen it in his own hand. We are the Uninvited: Syndicate assassins sworn to watch the watchers, and we have followed every contract you fulfilled.
ui.sanctum.lore.p2: The Syndicate's code is simple: we kill for the Syndicate, never for ourselves. Your ten targets were its auditors, and each of them had found the same thing: Master U. M. Bra's private ledger, and the money flowing into it.
ui.sanctum.lore.p3: He did not send you to protect the Syndicate. He sent you to protect himself, and when his books close, the apprentice is the last entry he will erase.
ui.sanctum.lore.p4: We have judged him, and we leave his contract to the one he used. Tonight, five shadows meet at his manor.
ui.sanctum.envelope.caption: Slipped in behind the photographs: a black envelope, addressed to S. H. Adow
ui.game.solved.umbra.title: The Umbra Conspiracy is closed
ui.game.solved.umbra.text: Master U. M. Bra lies on his own floor, and no eye saw who stood in the dark. The apprentice has become the ghost.

LORE.tutorial.1.TITLE: The Illusion of Justice
LORE.tutorial.1.TEXT: The inspector scribbled scapegoats on the board, a parlour trick we feed him for centuries.
LORE.tutorial.2.TITLE: The Ray Block
LORE.tutorial.2.TEXT: Aurora sat on a stool, and the Kitchen has two. Whichever she took, her gaze runs through the opening: that line is lit either way.
LORE.tutorial.3.TITLE: The Geometry of Panic
LORE.tutorial.3.TEXT: Dinah stood beside the safe. Aurora's row lights one side of it, so she takes the other: the safe blocks their view.
LORE.tutorial.4.TITLE: The Sanctuary
LORE.tutorial.4.TEXT: Every tile is lit but one. That single void in their vision is your sanctuary. Step into the shadows.
